elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly states: “Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.”

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are limited to Services used or ordered.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Customer “will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.”

elements.element: Any minimum purchase commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No minimum purchase commitment remains, so the condition requiring a commitment-duration limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum purchase commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No minimum purchase commitment remains to be reduced, so the condition triggering the required reduction right is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any shortfall against a minimum purchase commitment is resolved through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: No minimum purchase commitment or resulting shortfall remains, so the condition triggering a true-up mechanism is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position by eliminating the three-year take-or-pay commitment and limiting payment to Services used or ordered. The fallback protections are also satisfied because their triggering condition—a minimum purchase commitment—is absent. The revision is targeted, introduces no unrelated obligations, and does not contradict the stated commercial intent.
